title: Partitions With Equal Distinct Count
statement:
You are given a string `s` of lowercase English letters. A **partition** of `s` cuts it into one or more non-empty contiguous parts (substrings) whose concatenation is `s`. Two partitions are different if their sets of cut positions are different. Cutting nothing, so that the whole string is a single part, is also a valid partition.

A partition is **good** if every one of its parts contains the **same number of distinct characters**. That common number may differ from one good partition to another, but inside a single partition all parts must agree.

Count the good partitions of `s`. Because the count can be very large, print it modulo `1000000007`.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the number of good partitions modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: If every part has 1 distinct letter, each part must be a single letter (no two neighbours are equal), giving a|b|a|b. If every part has 2 distinct letters, the options are abab and ab|ab. Splits such as a|bab mix 1 and 2 distinct letters, so they are not good. Total 1 + 2 = 3.
With 1 distinct letter per part: a|a|b and aa|b. With 2 distinct letters per part: only the whole string aab. Total 3.
Every part always has exactly 1 distinct letter, so all partitions are good. There are 2 choices (cut or not) at each of the 2 gaps, so 4 partitions.

hints: A partition is good for exactly one value `d` (the common distinct count), so you can count good partitions separately for each `d` from 1 to 26 and add the results.

For a fixed `d`, let `dp[i]` be the number of ways to split the prefix of length `i` into parts that each have exactly `d` distinct letters. Then `dp[i]` is the sum of `dp[j]` over all `j` for which `s[j..i-1]` has exactly `d` distinct letters.

For a fixed end `i`, the distinct count of `s[j..i-1]` only grows as `j` moves left, so the valid `j` for each `d` form one contiguous range. The range boundaries come from the last occurrences of each letter, and prefix sums of `dp` turn each range sum into O(1).
